question: Which of the following early East India Company presidency headquarters or factories is NOT correctly matched with its geographical description in contemporary records?
options: Fort St. David - Masulipatnam (Coromandel Coast Factory)
wrong_fact: Fort St. David was located in Cuddalore, south of Pondicherry, not in Masulipatnam. It served as the temporary headquarters of the Madras Presidency from 1746 to 1752 after Madras fell to the French.
explanation: Fort St. David was built by the British at Cuddalore on the Coromandel Coast. Masulipatnam was home to an early EIC factory, but not Fort St. David. The others are correct presidencies: Fort William in Calcutta, Fort St. George in Madras, and Bombay Castle in Bombay.

question: Which of the following regional factories of the English East India Company is NOT correctly matched with the historical focus of its preserved record series?
options: Surat Factory Records - Early trade documentation of western India and the Red Sea trade (1612-1700s)
Anjengo Factory Records - Pepper trade and political relations with the rulers of Travancore
Bantam Factory Records - The early spice trade of the Malay Archipelago before the shift to India
Masulipatnam Factory Records - The opium trade records with China and North-East Asia
wrong_fact: Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam) was the earliest English settlement on the Coromandel Coast and its records deal with the textile and local Coromandel trade, not the opium trade with China, which was primarily conducted via Calcutta (Fort William) and Canton.
explanation: Masulipatnam records deal with the local textile and trade relations on the Coromandel Coast. Opium trade records are found in the Calcutta/Bengal Presidency records and the China factory records, not Masulipatnam.

question: Which of the following official record series of the East India Company is NOT correctly matched with its geographical origin or administrative archive in India?
options: Bengal Public Consultations - Fort William, Calcutta
Letters from Fort St. George - St. Helena Island Archive
Malabar Joint Commission Report - Calicut/Bombay Archive
wrong_fact: The 'Letters from Fort St. George' series represents the official correspondence of the Madras Presidency and is preserved in the Tamil Nadu Archives (Chennai) and the British Library (London), not the St. Helena Island Archive (which holds records of the EIC outpost on St. Helena in the Atlantic).
explanation: 'Letters from Fort St. George' are the main administrative and diplomatic letters sent from Madras. St. Helena had its own factory records as a strategic EIC transit stopover, but did not house Madras Presidency letters. Bengal consultations originated in Fort William, Bombay Diaries in Bombay Castle, and Malabar Joint Commission Reports in Malabar/Bombay.
